Approach: scan the grid; whenever an unvisited numeric 1 is found, use iterative DFS or BFS to count its island, exploring only up, down, left, and right. Mark cells visited when adding them to the worklist, and track the largest completed area without modifying the input.

Invariant: each land cell is counted at most once; each traversal counts exactly the land reachable from its starting cell, and the running maximum is the largest completed island.

Boundary cases: an empty grid or empty rows return 0; all zeros return 0; a single 1 returns 1; diagonal ones remain separate; an all-ones rectangular grid returns rows × columns. Bounds checks prevent traversal outside the grid.

Time: O(rows × columns). Auxiliary space: O(rows × columns) for visited cells and the worklist.

The screen shows Interview 88: interval intersections, with marker INTERVIEW-88-55ce5372eea6c80d. The task is to define solve(a,b), returning intersections of two sorted lists of disjoint closed intervals; touching endpoints count as a point intersection.

Use two pointers: compute start = max of the current starts and end = min of the current ends, and append [start, end] whenever start <= end. Advance the interval ending first, or both if their ends match, because that interval cannot overlap any later interval in the other list. The invariant is that all intersections involving discarded intervals have already been recorded.

Empty inputs return []; nonoverlapping intervals produce nothing; [[1,2]] and [[2,3]] produce [[2,2]]. Time is O(a.length + b.length), with O(1) auxiliary space excluding the result. The required interface has no imports, exports, or stdin/stdout handling.

Approach: use a sweep line over meeting starts and ends, tracking the active count and its maximum. Process ends before starts at the same time because intervals are half-open; ignore zero-duration intervals [t,t), which occupy no time. The maximum active count is the minimum number of rooms needed.

Invariant: after processing all events at time t, the active count equals the number of meetings satisfying start ≤ t < end. The recorded maximum is the greatest simultaneous occupancy seen so far: that many rooms are necessary, and reusing released rooms makes them sufficient.

Boundary cases: empty input or only zero-duration meetings returns 0; touching meetings reuse one room; overlapping, nested, or duplicate nonempty meetings count separately. Sort events to handle unsorted input. Time is O(n log n), with O(n) auxiliary space; reversed intervals are not specified by the attachment.

Approach: ignore empty lists and use a min-heap containing one current value from each nonempty list, while tracking their maximum. Evaluate [minimum, maximum], keeping the narrowest range and, on equal widths, the smaller left endpoint. Advance the list supplying the minimum; stop when that list is exhausted.

Invariant: the heap contains one representative from every participating list, so each candidate covers them all. Advancing the minimum is sufficient: keeping it while advancing other lists cannot reduce the maximum or improve the range.

Boundary cases: duplicates and negative values work normally; a shared value gives width zero; one nonempty list returns its smallest value twice. Empty lists impose no requirement, but TASK.md does not specify the result when all lists are empty or lists itself is empty—what should that return?

For N total values across k nonempty lists, time is O(N log(k + 1)) and auxiliary space is O(k).
